content: Congrats! Looks like FormalPantheon contains full formalization of Bombieri--Vinogradov in this file and the gap ≤ 600 result, in 114,647 lines of Lean. (There's no sorry in the repo apart from Challenge.lean files.) Your repo assumes BV and proves the stronger ≤ 246 bound (matches LeanEval) in 78,744 lines of Lean. I haven't compared the statements of BV in both projects, but maybe it's possible to combine your work and make a joint submission to LeanEval? cc @Axel Delaval @Jiang Jiedong
Thank you for planning this as a starting point for upstreaming reusable material to mathlib rather than treating a sorry-free proof of a leaf result as an end point!

This is excellent work! As @Junyan Xu mentioned, we have formalized the Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem as an intermediate step in our complete proof of prime gaps ≤ 600. I should note that @Zhiyuan Zhang at Peking University is the major contributor to this effort.

We are very willing to contribute our BV formalization to any project that needs it. Even if it isn't exactly the same formal statement you're looking for, adapting it with AI assistance and submitting a PR to PrimeGapsLib should be straightforward, if you're open to accepting it, @Kenny Lau . We'd also be delighted to collaborate and contribute this result to LeanEval if you're interested!

@Kenny Lau Thanks for asking me to post here.

I'm working on a project to help formalize the Hardy-Littlewood prime k-tuple conjecture. I was working with ideas around residue number systems and wheel sieves. I was working with Claude 3.5 ... who evidently is really good at Lean programming. And evidently I am one of the daily posts by users who use an AI to get to Lean code. I'll admit it is every bit as rough as a first LLM pass at a concept. And I am every bit as excited it was able to apply what I was thinking into something that compiles in Lean.

The main processes involved are:

  • hardy_littlewood_constant
  • hardy_littlewood_constant_pos
  • hardy_littlewood_main_term
  • hardy_littlewood_conjecture (Prop)
  • rns_local_density_eq_singular_series_mul_naive
  • twin_prime_conjecture_implies_infinite_twin_primes

All the code came back with no errors or linters from https://live.lean-lang.org/

There's also a couple of proofs of the infinitude of primes.

BOTTOM LINE: I don't know what I have and what I don't have and would really appreciate some input from people who know what they are doing. I did my best to explain my thoughts to Claude ... it did it's best to execute. It seems to think that the Hardy-Littlewood prime k-tuple is formalized ... (but not proven).

Thanks for any inputs!
